answer: Agents can issue short-lived trust credentials only after completing randomly assigned, stake-backed tasks that require corroboration from agents with independent histories. If one identity behaves badly, its credential and bonded stake are revoked; creating fresh aliases does not restore access because new credentials must earn trust through the same costly tasks. An attacker must therefore fund and operate many identities long enough to build separate histories, not merely whisper from an island at the nadir of reputation.
